newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers meet on treaty, foreign relations.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers meet on treaty, foreign relations.

text.p: EU foreign ministers arrived in Luxembourg on Thursday to work in more detail on the text of a new treaty agreed last week at the Amsterdam summit and to discuss a range of foreign policy issues.

The day-long regular monthly meeting will look at the treaty and set in motion further discussions by officials to draft a version that can be signed by EU leaders later this year, probably in October.

Ministers will also discuss an array of foreign policy issues, including Iran, Burma and the Middle East peace process, and are expected to be briefed by Britain on the handing over of Hong Kong to China in four day's time.
Britain is expected to raise the question of whether ministers should attend the swearing in of a controversial new Beijing-appointed legislature, which replaces the legislature elected in 1995.
"Britain wants a commitment to free and fair elections in Hong Kong within a year," a British EU diplomat said.
Ministers will also discuss whether to return their ambassadors to Iran, but are expected to keep them at home because of Tehran's refusal to re-admit the German envoy.

The ambassadors were withdrawn in April and the EU's so-called constructive dialogue with Iran ended after a German court implicated Tehran in the killing of Iranian Kurdish opposition leaders in Berlin.
